title: Missing-Value Handling
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of missing-value handling and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply detecting missing values with is.na() in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Missing-Value Handling is part of Data Types, Values, and Basic Objects. Start with detecting missing values with is.na() and connect it to the worked example and expected result.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: NA represents missing information; arithmetic and comparisons can propagate missingness. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Compare is.na(x) with x == NA and explain why they are not interchangeable. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Missing-Value Handling
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 26: Missing-Value Handling
example_values <- c(7, NA, 9)
is.na(example_values)

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For missing-value handling, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Removing rows before measuring how much information is missing.
common_mistakes.why: Missingness or outliers may be systematic and can bias the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Count affected rows, state the rule, compare before/after summaries and keep an audit trail.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating every repeated key as an accidental duplicate.
common_mistakes.why: Repeated rows may represent repeated events or valid measurements.
common_mistakes.fix: Define the expected key grain and review examples before deleting records.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing categories or units without documenting the transformation.
common_mistakes.why: Silent standardization makes results difficult to reproduce.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the mapping rule and add a validation check.
